messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>

Cc: 
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-quarter signal review & proposed pivots

Team —

Attached is a compact "signal snapshot" for Q3 that consolidates delivery velocity, latency SLOs, and the top three lagging experiment cohorts (Q3_signal_snapshot_v2.pdf). High level: we are tracking mixed performance on the Optimize initiative (tokens-per-second efficiency) and a growing tail in RLHF evaluation pass rates for the cust-embedding workload.

Recommendation (two options):
- Option A (narrow pivot, low risk): Pause noncritical minor feature rollouts for two weeks, reallocate one infra engineer to the Optimize backlog, and apply quantization profile B to the 2x test pool. Expected outcome: restore tokens/sec targets in 2–3 weeks; minimal customer-visible changes.
- Option B (bolder, medium risk): Re-scope the Optimize OKR to focus on model-variant routing and KV-cache improvements, pull forward the Q4 routing prototype and run a 2-week live experiment. Expected outcome: larger upside on unit cost but requires temporary throttling on non-critical Dedicated capacity testing.

Dependencies I need alignment on before Friday (EOD PT):
1) Engineering headcount swap: approval to reassign one infra engineer (owner: Markus)
2) Product prioritization: signoff to delay two planned minor features (owner: Laura)
3) CS communication plan if we enable temporary throttling (owner: Vivek)

I've attached a short re-scope table (proposed_re-scope_table.xlsx) with estimated impact points and a first-pass runbook for the low-risk Option A. Please reply with: (a) which option you prefer, (b) learnings/risks I should add to the runbook, and (c) who will own the dependency items above.

Thanks — happy to sync live if it's easier.

— Olga
Olga Petrov
VP, Platform
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Q3_signal_snapshot_v2.pdf (pdf, 420KB); proposed_re-scope_table.xlsx (xlsx, 48KB)

Subject: Re: Mid-quarter signal review & proposed pivots

Thanks, Olga — useful concise pack. My preference is Option A unless Laura sees a compelling product reason to take a bolder approach. Two quick asks I want included in the runbook before I sign off on reassigning infra:

- Metric targets: please add an explicit tokens/sec recovery target and a customer-impact SLO delta (e.g., p95 latency increase tolerated).
- Risk register: add a short contingency if quantization profile B regresses eval pass rates (roll back trigger + rollback owner).

If we get those in writing I can commit the infra resource today and slot the handover into the cadenced infra sync.

On the staffing note: Markus (infra) will own the reassignment; once Olga confirms I'm ok to move him tomorrow morning.

On Fri I have a 1:1 with the infra lead; will confirm timelines there.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-quarter signal review & proposed pivots

Appreciate the clear options, Olga. I lean toward Option B if we can secure CS gating (Vivek) and a measured rollout so we don't create support noise. The reason: the embedding workload's degradation looks like a routing/variant mismatch more than pure infra. If true, routing fixes unlock both latency and token-efficiency simultaneously.

Practical asks if we go Option B:
- I need a prioritized list of the two minor features we would delay (so I can message PMs and engineering leads).
- A 2-week experiment plan with success criteria (preferably split into quick safety checks after 48 hours + full metric window at day 14).
- A risk communication draft for customers (one-paragraph blurb) — I can take point on that once we agree the features.

If the team prefers Option A for speed, I'm ok with that too; just need the feature list and confirmation of rollback windows.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick confirmations from CS perspective:

- We can support Option B but only if the experiment has an explicit customer-safe gating plan. We will not allow any global throttles without a targeted subset and pre-agreed rollback triggers.
- If we do Option A, CS needs a one-paragraph notice and a named contact for any customer escalations (I recommend Priya from Enterprise CS temporarily).

Decision: lean to Option B with constraints.
Action items:
- Olga: finalize experiment plan with 48h safety checks + explicit success metrics; add tokens/sec targets and rollback triggers in the runbook.
- Markus: prepare infra handover doc and identify the engineer for temporary reassignment.
- Laura: list the two features that would be pushed and draft the customer blurb; capture PM approvals.

I'll coordinate with Priya_natarajan and the Enterprise CS rotation roster if we end up doing A. Once we have the runbook updates, let's do a 20-min sync tomorrow at 9:30am PT for final sign-off.
